newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria, Kuwait agree to boost trade exchange.
newsitem.headline: Syria, Kuwait agree to boost trade exchange.

text.p: Syria and Kuwait agreed on Tuesday to boost their trade exchanges and the Gulf state will help finance the expansion of Syria's telephone network, Kuwait's Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan said.
Rodhan told Reuters that a joint Syrian-Kuwaiti ministerial committee that met in Damascus from Monday also decided that plans for establishing a joint airline be discussed in technical committees.
He said bilateral trade had increased since 1995 when Syrian exports to Kuwait were worth $66 million and Kuwaiti exports to Syria $15 million, and the joint committee agreed to boost it further.
"I would not say we want it to go to $200 million or $300 million per year because we believe...the volume of trade could be even bigger," Rodhan said.

He said Kuwait's Development Fund, which has given Syria 21 soft loans totalling $884 million, would co-finance some new infrastructure projects in Syria including the expansion of its telephone network. He gave no cost figures.
A $200 million Kuwaiti investment company established recently in Syria was in the final stages of preparations for building a five-star hotel in Damascus, the minister said.
It was also discussing the construction of a flat glass plant and a cement factory in partnership with a foreign company, Rodhan added.
Rodhan and Syrian Deputy Prime Minister for economic affairs Salim Yassin co-chaired meetings of the joint commission.
